name: Hidane Oracle Corpus
description: The official Cloud Firestore emulator's answers that hidane records, replays and compares: every recording, how it was made, the release it was made against, and how its answers are compared. See docs/oracle-corpus.md.

recordings.counted: each commit over each transport it was recorded over, and each step that writes to or reads after another database
recordings.compared: in full: the first error's code and message, the number of write results or `:batchWrite`'s statuses, a read's status, names found or missing; a failed precondition without its message (it prints the official emulator's internal key); the cases the test lists in `KNOWN` (array unions of arrays and of vectors with NaN) and the steps in `DIFFERS` (writes to another database, which hidane refuses, and the reads that follow) as intentionally different

recordings.counted: each recorded message the tests check hidane's against (they replay no case as a whole); recorded over REST
recordings.compared: in full: the code and the message (a stored version's timestamps masked)

oracle.evidence: no header; tools/oracle/ names only cloud-firestore-emulator v1.22.0 at the commit that added it

recordings.compared: an error in full (status and message); a commit on its status; a read in part: the order of every field, nested ones included, and which commit its `updateTime` names, not the values

recordings.counted: each case (a paged case is one)
recordings.compared: in full: the names of every page, or the code and message

an error in full (code and message), but a failed precondition on its code (its message prints the official emulator's internal key, an intentional difference); a commit in full (its number of write results and the commit each one's update time comes from, or that it has none; the times themselves differ from run to run), in part where they hold transform results, which are not compared; a read in part (the fields and their order), a missing document on its code
a commit in full (its transform results, server times as the request time, or the code and message); a read in part (the document's fields), a missing document on its code
an error in full (status and message); results in part: every aggregate value with its type, not `done`, which gRPC does not carry
in full: the documents' names and fields but the vector (as the recording keeps them), the aggregate values, or the status and message

recordings.counted: each query but the `findNearest` one; recorded over REST
recordings.compared: in full: each response's document, `skippedResults` and `done`, the fields of projected documents, or the status and message
in full: the outcome as the recording summarises it

recordings.counted: each step with an outcome, except those of the scenario marked `slow`
recordings.compared: as each step's `compare` marks it; without a mark in full (status, message, elapsed time to 0.5 s and the result, not transaction IDs)
as each step's `compare` marks it; without a mark in full (the response's token, write results and commit time as the recording summarises them, the error, the elapsed time)
in full: status, every header but `date`, `content-length` and `connection`, and the body
as each case's `compare` marks it: `exact` in full (status, content type and body byte for byte, server times, IDs and tokens masked), `status` on its status and content type
in full: status, frames and messages (session IDs, times and tokens masked); a long-polling read in part (its first data and whether it ended: where the `noop`s fall depends on timing)

oracle.evidence: no header; tools/oracle/ names only cloud-firestore-emulator v1.22.0 at the commit that added it

recordings.counted: each condition or ruleset decided; recorded over REST
recordings.compared: an allow and a compile error in full; a denial as decision and reasons (the entries of one evaluation where the official emulator lists two); a denied batch on its decision only (in part); the official 500s, which hidane answers with an evaluation error, as intentionally different

recordings.counted: each step of each case (registrations and writes over REST, gRPC and the Write stream), in the three runs: with a Functions emulator, without, and with one that does not listen
recordings.compared: in full: the status, every request the Functions emulator received (method, path, content type and `ce-*` headers, the v1 body byte for byte and the v2 body decoded, times and IDs as labels), and every `WARNING` about events. Intentionally different: steps with v2 events (`ce-source` names the project once), events for writes that change nothing, after `POST /reset`, and a v2 trigger without a database; in part (in any order): a deleted path or a cleared database
in full: status, content type and body
